name: simple
description: A language-agnostic Claude Code setup: five role-based agents each pinned to the right model, 49 path-triggered rule packs covering 17 languages, 6 front-end frameworks, 16 ORMs, 5 databases and the infrastructure around them, a project memory vault you can open in Obsidian, two hooks, a status line and side panes drawn by the plugin itself (a mod), and the method for measuring a plugin before adopting it.

statusline.title: Status line
statusline.description: Draw the two-row status line under the prompt: directory, git, pull request and CI; model, effort, context, cache, cost and plan limits.

statuslineAbovePrompt.title: Status line above the prompt
statuslineAbovePrompt.description: Draw the status line in the band above the prompt instead of under it.

statuslineWeekly.title: Status line weekly totals
statuslineWeekly.description: Show the 7-day token totals per model family. Runs python3 at most every two minutes.

statuslinePr.title: Status line pull request and CI
statuslinePr.description: Show the branch's pull request (review state) and its CI in the status line. Asks GitHub through one read-only gh api graphql call, shared with the side panes, every two minutes (every minute while checks run).

workbench.title: Side panes
workbench.description: /workbench opens two side panes. Work: this branch's ticket, pull request (reviews, checks, merge state) and CI, the repository's open pull requests, your review requests and assigned issues. Session: MCP calls, agents, permission checks and a log. While Work is open, its GitHub part shares the one gh api graphql call.

workbenchAutoOpen.title: Open the side panes by themselves
workbenchAutoOpen.description: Open Work and Session beside the transcript once per session, in a fullscreen terminal at least 144 columns wide (110 once you have opened them yourself). Closing them stops this until you open them again with /workbench.
